Hi Michael —

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Dedicated last week. Our execs gave a soft thumbs-up to proceed with a conversion from Hosted to Dedicated for our main inference traffic, contingent on a short validation run and a predictable cutover timeline. High-level asks from our side:

- A deterministic sizing proposal for initial capacity ( GPUs + memory / per-pool ) based on our traffic profile (attached).
- A short validation window where we can run mirrored production traffic and measure latency, tails, and throughput.
- A proposed cutover weekend and rollback criteria.

We are targeting a production cutover the week of May 22 if everything looks green — can Redwood support a sanity run prior to that? I attached our traffic_sample.jsonl and the current contract redlines for reference.

Two quick notes about our traffic: peak surrounding launches is highly spiky (bursts to ~250 RPS for 3–8 minutes), token mix skews short (avg 24 tokens, 99th ~240) but we have a small 1% profile of long-form requests.

Can you outline what you need from us to scope GPUs and a validation cadence?

— Samantha
Samantha Holt
Head of Product, SlateFlight

Samantha —

Appreciate the samples and redline. Yes — we can run a short, mirrored validation and propose a cutover weekend. To scope GPUs and a safe rehearsal cadence we need three quick artifacts (feel free to send as links):

1) 7-day peak-per-minute RPS (UTC) split by endpoint and request type (in practice a small CSV is fine).
2) Token-distribution histogram (you provided a sample but full distribution helps).
3) Any latency / SLO targets you must meet (p50/p90/p95/p99 token latency targets).

Our proposed approach:
- Capacity sizing: produce a conservative starting fleet (N gpus) + 20% burst pool. We typically express sizing as: GPU-count / model-variant lanes / KV-cache hot nodes.
- Validation plan: 72-hour mirrored replay in a staging slice + controlled spike test (10x burst for 5 minutes) to exercise tails and cache behaviour.
- Acceptance criteria: sustained throughput within 5% of upstream hosted baseline, p95 latency within agreed SLO, no more than 0.5% error responses, memory/KV eviction within safe bounds.
- Cutover weekend: a two-phase cutover — staged traffic ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30–60 minute hold points and automatic rollback triggers.

Ben and Marissa are copied — they will propose GPU counts and an estimated runbook once we have the RPS and token histogram. If you can confirm the May 12–14 rehearsal window and a May 21–22 cutover weekend we’ll lock resources and schedule the staging slice.

Action items (from Redwood):
- I will populate the capacity_template_v2.xlsx and send the first pass by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben will draft a staging runbook and rollback triggers.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick engineering note / initial sizing take —

Based on the sample and the described burst profile, my working assumptions:
- Baseline sustained RPS: 60–80 (avg) with bursts to 250 for short windows.
- Model: opt-13b-quant (approx 30ms token generation p50 on A100-like runtime in hosted baseline).

Conservative starting fleet (proposal):
- 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs in primary pool (handles baseline + KV hot partitioning).
- 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs as burst nodes behind an autoscale buffer (handles the 3–8 minute spikes).
- Staging mirror: 2 GPUs to run mirrored traffic and enable KV/cache warming without impacting prod.

Planned tests for the 72-hr validation:
1) Steady-state run at 100% mirrored load for 24h.
2) Repeated short bursts (simulate 10x RPS for 5m) to validate throttle & cache.
3) Long-form request soak to exercise KV eviction and memory pressure.

I'll put numbers into the capacity_template_v2.xlsx and send it back by EOD. If SlateFlight can confirm token histograms and peak CSV today we can probably lock the staging window May 12–14 and schedule the cutover rehearsal May 18–19.

— Ben

Following up with a consolidated plan and owners now that we have the peak CSV and token histogram. Summary timeline and owners:

- May 11: Staging network peering confirmed (SlateFlight Cloud Ops) — owner: Samantha
- May 12–14: 72-hour mirrored validation (Staging slice: 2 GPUs) — owner: Ben (runbook + validation scripts)

Acceptance criteria (final version to be in the runbook):

- p95 token latency <= agreed SLO (TBD in runbook).
- Error rate <= 0.5%.
- Redis/KV eviction rate acceptable (no data loss affecting inference correctness).
